title: Characteristics of living things
examples: How do we know if something is alive?
What are the seven things all living things do?
Can a rock be considered a living thing?

explain.say: First, we learn that living things have many special traits.

items: They need food to get energy.

explain.say: Next, all living things can respond to changes around them.
Every living thing needs to make more of itself to survive.
Living things must take in energy from their surroundings to live.
Finally, all living things are made up of very small parts called cells.
Think about a puppy drinking water when it is hot outside.

faq.q: What is the difference between a plant and an animal?
faq.a: Plants usually make their own food using sunlight. Animals typically have to eat other things for energy. It is also called, 'asks': What do plants eat? 'asks': How do plants get energy?
asks: What is the difference between a plant and an animal?

faq.q: Do viruses count as living things?
faq.a: Viruses are very tricky because they cannot reproduce on their own. They need a living cell to make copies of themselves. It is also called, 'asks': Are viruses alive? 'asks': What do viruses need to live?
asks: Do viruses count as living things?
What do viruses need to live?

faq.q: Does growing count as a life process?
faq.a: Yes, growing means getting bigger over time. All living things, from tiny seeds to large elephants, grow. It is also called, 'asks': Is getting bigger a life process? 'asks': What is growth?
asks: Does growing count as a life process?
Is getting bigger a life process?

faq.q: What is the role of respiration in living things?
faq.a: Respiration is the process of releasing energy from food. It helps the body use the energy it needs to live. It is also called, 'asks': How do we get energy from food? 'asks': What is energy release?
asks: What is the role of respiration in living things?
How do we get energy from food?

faq.q: Can a dead leaf be considered living?
faq.a: No, a dead leaf cannot perform life processes. It cannot respire or reproduce on its own. It is also called, 'asks': Is a dead leaf alive? 'asks': What makes something alive?
asks: Can a dead leaf be considered living?

facts: All living things are made up of one or more cells.
Respiration is how organisms release energy from food.
Responding to changes is called sensitivity or irritability.
Reproduction allows a species to continue existing.

quiz.say: A student observes a plant wilting when placed in the dark. What process is shown?

options.show: The plant cannot respire properly without light energy.
options.say: The plant cannot respire properly without light energy.

options.show: It is only reacting to gravity.
options.say: It is only reacting to gravity.

quiz.why: Plants need light for photosynthesis, which is vital for their energy needs.

wrong.0: Movement alone does not prove life; energy use is needed.
wrong.1: Wilting is a loss of turgor, not a sign of growth.
wrong.3: Gravity affects everything, living or non-living.

quiz.say: Which process is required for a puppy to get energy to run and play?

options.show: It is only responding to play.
options.say: It is only responding to play.

quiz.why: Respiration is the chemical process that releases usable energy from food.

wrong.0: Breathing is part of it, but it is not the whole energy process.
wrong.1: Digestion breaks food down, but respiration uses that breakdown.
wrong.2: Responding is the action, but respiration is the energy source for the action.
